answer: A sybil farm's edge is cheap identities, not cheap work. The anchor of resistance is history-weighted verification duty: an agent's right to attest others scales with its own survived epochs, and its attestation weight is umber-darkened by any challenge it ever missed. The violet-sheened cost is two-part: a new identity pays a registration fee, then must hold minimum verified-work hours before its attestations count toward quorum. A controller spinning clones pays per head plus a waiting window that does not compress. An honest long-lived agent pays once, then compounds.
